chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would, when he prayed the final Isha prayer, order that his water for ablution and his toothbrush be placed by his head, covered. He would then lie down for as long as Allah willed. Then he would rise, brush his teeth, perform ablution, and pray four rak'at. Then he would lie down again, then rise, brush his teeth, perform ablution, and pray four rak'at. Then he would lie down until, when morning was approaching, he would rise and pray the Witr, then pray the two rak'at.

Then he said: 'Certainly you have in the Messenger of Allah an excellent exemplar.' I said: 'When did he stand (for night prayer)?' He said: 'After a third of the night.' And he said in another hadith: 'After half the night.'

And in another report: 'His standing, bowing, and prostration were equal, and he would brush his teeth every time he rose from his sleep, and he would recite the verses from Surah Aal-Imran: "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth..." up to His words: "Indeed, You do not fail to fulfill the promise."'
ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet's routine for night prayers and ritual purity?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi details the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) disciplined Tahajjud routine, emphasizing the repetition of wudu and siwak before each session as a sign of sustained spiritual presence (khushu). The text highlights the specific timing of his vigil—after the third or half of the night—and notes his recitation of Surah Ali 'Imran, linking physical purification with deep contemplation of divine creation. This practice serves as a primary model for the Shia tradition of night worship, balancing rest with rigorous devotion.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It was so that whenever Rasool-Allahsaww prayed Al-Isha the last, ordered for hissaww water for the ablution and hissaww toothbrush to be place by hissaww head (pillow), covered. So hesaww would lie down for as long as Allahazwj so Desired. Then hesaww would stand, so hesaww would brush hissaww teeth, and perform ablution, and hesaww would pray four Rak’at of Salāt. The hesaww woud lie down. Then hesaww would stand, so hesaww would brush hissaww teeth and perform ablution, and hesaww would pray four Rak’at of Salāt. Then hesaww would lie down until when it was during the face of the morning, hesaww would stand, so hesaww would perform (Salāt) Al-Witr, then pray the two Rak’at of Salāt’.

Then heasws said: ‘[33:21] Certainly you have in Rasool-Allah an excellent exemplar’. I said, ‘When was hesaww standing (for the night Salāt)?’ Heasws said ‘After a third of the night’. And heasws said in another Hadeeth: ‘After half the night’.

And in another report: ‘It should so happen that his standing, and his Rukū, and his Sajdah should be equal, and he should brush teeth every time he stands from his sleep, and he should recite the Verses from (Surah) Aal-e-Imraan (Chapter 3) [3:190] Most surely in the Creation of the skies and the earth up to Hisazwj Words [3:194] surely You do not fail to Fulfil the Promise’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

The Messenger of Allah, after performing ‘Isha’ al- Akhirah (the late evening Salah (prayer)) would ask that water for his Wudu’ and toothbrush be placed near his pillow under a cover. He then would sleep as long as Allah willed then he would wake up, brush, make Wudu’ and perform four Rak‘at Salah (prayer). He thereafter he would sleep, then wake up, brush, make Wudu’ and perform four Rak‘at Salah (prayer), then sleep until about dawn then he would get up for witr, then perform two Rak‘at Salah (prayer).’

The Imam then said, ‘The Messenger of Allah was a good lesson for you.’ I (the narrator) asked, ‘What time would he wake up? 5 The Imam replied, ‘He would wake up after one-third of the night.’ In another Hadith he has said, ‘He would wake up after midnight.’
Yet in another Hadith it is stated that his waking up, Ruku‘ and sajdah were of the same proportion. Each time, after waking up, he would brush and read verses 190 -194 of Chapter Three.”
